tl;dr: 20 is a nice round number but 19 is prime…prime time to experience life outside the bubble. After 19 years at Google, it’s time to go.

After 19 years at Google, I’ve decided to see what life is like on the outside. Now that the team has handed off the 2nd edition of the Site Reliability Engineering Book to O’Reilly’s production process, it felt like this was the right time to embark on a new adventure. 

I’ve been exercising my science brain since I earned my Ph.D. in Chemistry over 25 years ago. I want to take some time to exercise my creative brain in this next chapter. I plan to lean into various writing projects and double-down on my love of doors from my home base in Lisbon, Portugal. When one door closes, there is always another one (or 1000 \o/) to photograph!

Of course, I still plan to fly the flag for SRE best practices, especially as the SRE Book 2nd edition comes out later this year. Perhaps I’ll see you at GOTO Copenhagen, SREcon EMEA in Dublin, or Øredev in Malmö before we close out 2026! 

It has been an honor and a privilege to be a part of the Google community for so long. Whether we worked together for years, just a moment in time, or even indirectly, I’d love it if you’d leave a comment here (or DM me if you’d prefer not to share publicly) with a memory so we can reminisce.

For now, I’ll leave you with 19 Things I’ve Found to be True Over 19 Years in Tech ⬇️
